hints: Notice that ice, water and steam are all the same substance, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so start by thinking about moles of gas and the ideal gas law.
Work out the moles first from 1.00 g of water using $n = m/M_r$ with $M_r = 18.0$.
Put those moles into $pV = nRT$ with temperature in kelvin and pressure in pascals, then convert your answer from $\text{m}^3$ to $\text{dm}^3$.
walkthrough:
**Find the moles of water**

Heating ice to 323 degrees C just turns it into gaseous $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, steam. The mass stays 1.00 g.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r} = \frac{1.00}{18.0} = 0.0556 \text{ mol}$$

**Prepare T and p in the correct units**

The gas equation needs absolute temperature and SI pressure. Add 273 to the Celsius temperature.

$$T = 323 + 273 = 596 \text{ K}$$
$$p = 101 \text{ kPa} = 101000 \text{ Pa}$$

**Apply the ideal gas equation**

Steam at this high temperature behaves as an ideal gas, so use $pV = nRT$ with $R = 8.31 \text{ J mol}^{-1} \text{ K}^{-1}$.

$$V = \frac{nRT}{p} = \frac{0.0556 \times 8.31 \times 596}{101000}$$

**Calculate and convert to dm3**

This gives volume in $\text{m}^3$. Multiply by 1000 to get $\text{dm}^3$.

$$V = 0.00272 \text{ m}^3 = 0.00272 \times 1000 = 2.7 \text{ dm}^3$$

options.A: Incorrect. 0.27 is 10 times too small. This comes from a power-of-ten slip, for example multiplying $\text{m}^3$ by 100 instead of 1000 to get $\text{dm}^3$. Always check: $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000 \text{ dm}^3$.
options.B: Incorrect. About 1.3 to 1.5 $\text{dm}^3$ is what you get if you forget to convert Celsius to kelvin and use $T = 323$ in $pV = nRT$. Gas temperature must always be absolute temperature, so 323 degrees C is 596 K.
options.C: Correct. 0.0556 mol of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at 596 K and 101 kPa occupies about $2.72 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$, which is 2.7 $\text{dm}^3$.
options.D: Incorrect. About 48 $\text{dm}^3$ is what you get if you use 1.00 mol instead of 1.00 g. You must first divide by $M_r$ of water, 18.0, to get 0.0556 mol before using $pV = nRT$.
